did_you_know.text: Did you know? The sons of the prophets told Elisha that their place of residence was too small, so they asked to expand it near the Jordan.
Did you know? The iron that fell into the water had been borrowed, so the man distressed by its loss cried out, “Oh no, my master! It was borrowed!”
Did you know? Elisha asked where the iron had fallen, threw a piece of wood into the spot, and the iron floated to the surface of the water.
Did you know? The king of Israel was repeatedly warned about the Aramean ambushes—“not once or twice”—thanks to Elisha’s warnings.
Did you know? When the king of Aram discovered that Elisha was thwarting his plans, he was told that the prophet was in Dothan, so he sent a large army there.
Did you know? After Elisha prayed, his servant’s eyes were opened, and he saw the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire surrounding Elisha.
Did you know? Elisha led the Aramean soldiers, who had been struck with blindness, to Samaria—the city they supposedly intended to reach.
Did you know? Elisha stopped the king of Israel from killing the Aramean soldiers and ordered him to give them bread and water and send them back to their master.
Did you know? The siege of Samaria caused extreme famine: a donkey’s head sold for eighty shekels of silver, and a small measure of dove droppings sold for five shekels.
Did you know? When the king of Israel heard the woman’s shocking story, he tore his clothes, and it was revealed that he was wearing sackcloth next to his skin beneath his clothes.
